Oct 4 : Britain's Elfyn Evans finally won the World Rally Championship (WRC) title with Toyota on Sunday after years of finishing runner-up. The Welshman had been second overall five times in the last six years but emerged triumphant after a nail-biting final stage duel with teammate Oliver Solberg in the season-ending Italian round in Sardinia. Welshman Evans is the first British world rally champion since Englishman Richard Burns in 2001 and only the third since Scottish driver Colin McRae became the nation's first in 1995. Sweden's Solberg, son of Norway's 2003 champion Petter, won the rally and ended the season as runner-up.

Source: Reuters

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : Lewis Hamilton said he had mixed emotions after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia where he started second on the grid but dropped to 18th when a tyre gamble went wrong before fighting to finish third in a chaotic, rain-hit race on Sunday. After rain delayed the start of the race by more than 90 minutes, Hamilton was one of the few drivers who switched from intermediate tyres to slicks on a track that was still drying. The Briton had a slow start and then found himself going backwards, falling as low as 18th, but he opted to stick with his strategy despite Ferrari calling him back into the pits for a tyre change. Hamilton then carved his way through the field as the track dried up while safety cars also came to his rescue, with the veteran eventually overtaking Red Bull's Isack Hadjar in the dying stages to secure a podium behind Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli.

"As a team, we ended up taking that soft (tyre) and at the end of the pit lane, these two (Verstappen and Antonelli) took off their (tyre) blankets and my heart just sank, because I knew straight away that we were in trouble," Hamilton told reporters. "As we pulled out, all the spray came out the back of Max's car and I was like, 'Okay, I'm done. My race is really in trouble'. "We made the decision to live with it. As everyone was overtaking me, they (Ferrari) said, 'Should we stop?' I said, 'No, we've already waited another 26 seconds. What's the difference'." But as the track dried and safety car deployments played into his hands, Hamilton began a remarkable recovery drive as he gave Hadjar chase for fourth place, before George Russell's retirement gave him a shot at a podium. "I just waited for the track to dry and once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great. Then after that, really good pit stops from my guys in the garage," Hamilton added. "And then a good strategy. So for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that's what was going to be the case. I'm really, really grateful." His teammate Charles Leclerc also salvaged fourth place for Ferrari and he conceded that was the best they could have achieved considering how much faster Red Bull and Mercedes were. "Honestly, the first part of the race, everything that could have gone wrong went wrong. And on the second part, everything that could have gone right went our way," Leclerc said. "So at the end of the day, I prefer it that way than the other way around. We were P4 today and I honestly think that with a normal race we would have finished P3 and P4. The two guys in front were just way too quick for us. "Lewis had quite a good pace. I struggled a lot with the car, which we're looking into. I had a good feeling on Friday, good feeling until Q2, and then Q3 I started to lose out. Today the race was very tricky."

Source: Reuters

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : George Russell's Formula One title hopes took a crushing blow when his Mercedes ground to a halt with a power unit failure five laps from the finish, turning what looked like a certain podium into heartbreak at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday. The British driver was running in a strong position to claim valuable championship points when the second safety car emerged for Alex Albon's Williams, which was stuck in the gravel. But as the field prepared for a thrilling finale behind the safety car, Russell - who was third behind eventual race winner Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli - suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he climbed out. "You've almost got to laugh, it's beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame," Russell said.

"The podium looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race. But not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling." The retirement meant Russell's championship deficit grew from 66 points to 84 behind Antonelli. "I don't need to say I think it's (championship hopes) gone or whatever, but of course it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality," Russell added. "I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side... It's a real shame." Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirmed it was a power unit failure on Russell's car. "I'm so massively annoyed. I'm not in a happy place," Wolff said. "First of all we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will." With the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc finishing third and fourth, Mercedes' lead in the constructors' standings is now 151 points. "We had such an advantage (with) two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky," Wolff added. "And to make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points. "So as much as I love to be here, when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest."

Source: Reuters

SYDNEY, Oct 4 : Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries as the Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the National Rugby League final on Sunday, securing the foundation club a 16th title. Nawaqanitawase, who could represent Australia at both the league and union World Cups over the next 12 months, crossed either side of halftime to help crush Newcastle hopes of a massive upset in front of a crowd of 80,814 at Stadium Australia. Newcastle were looking to take the title back to their industrial port city for the first time since 2001 and scored the first two tries of the contest through Francis Manuleleua and skipper Kalyn Ponga to take an early 12-0 lead. Nawaqanitawase, playing the final game of his two-year stint at the Roosters before his return to rugby union, cut the deficit from a clever kick and chase five minutes before the break, however.

Newcastle defended several sets on their own line at the start of the second half but Roosters centre Billy Smith forced his way over in the 47th minute for a converted try that locked up the scores at 12-12. Sam Walker put the Sydney side in front for the first time with a penalty seven minutes later, and Nawaqanitawase added his second try in the right corner before the hour mark to extend the lead to 18-12. Experienced five-eighth Daly Cherry-Evans, playing his last NRL game before his switch to England's Super League, slotted a field goal to extend the advantage to seven points but the Knights found a second wind in the remaining 11 minutes. Summoning the spirit of last week's sensational win over the Penrith Panthers with 12 men that got them to the final, they forced their way upfield and winger Greg Marzhew crossed for a converted try that made it a one-point game with four minutes on the clock. The Roosters, one of the two clubs remaining from the first season of what became the NRL in 1908, held on, however, to secure their first title since 2019 and fourth under long-term coach Trent Robinson. "Credit to the Knights, they fought for 80 minutes there," said Nawaqanitawase. "This is going to last me a lifetime, it's sad to go but I love everyone here, I love all the boys, and let's celebrate this win, far out."

Source: Reuters

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday for his first victory of the season after the race start was delayed by more than 90 minutes due to treacherous conditions at the Sepang International Circuit. Verstappen was the last driver to win in Sepang in 2017 before it was taken off the calendar and the Dutchman, who had also taken pole, gave Red Bull a first victory with their own power unit despite an early setback when he lost the lead before turn one. "It's a really nice one after the year that we've had and the progression that we've made. So I'm incredibly proud of everyone. It is super nice to win here," said Verstappen. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second for Mercedes and now has an 84-point lead over his closest rival and teammate George Russell, who was third when he retired with a suspected power unit issue with five laps remaining.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished third despite a tyre gamble that had dropped the Briton down to 18th at the start of the race. "Obviously, we had the wrong call at the beginning, which was so difficult and I could see everyone just pulling away," Hamilton said. "I thought that was kind of race over for us, but I just kept my head down. The guys did a great job with the pit stops." Antonelli held on to second from Hamilton in the closing laps. "Today was the maximum we could have done... On our side, a lot of work to do," Antonelli said. "We've been struggling a bit more than usual, but still really happy to come away with P2." The last four laps were a straight shootout for podium places after a lengthy safety car period and that was when Hamilton, who had been chasing Red Bull's Isack Hadjar for several laps, made his move. Charles Leclerc, who had also been closer to the back of the grid at the start of the race amid the chaos of a wet track, salvaged fourth for Ferrari when he overtook Hadjar with two laps to go. Hadjar finished fifth ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Liam Lawson was seventh while Fernando Alonso was eighth for Aston Martin, their best result of the season. FIRST WET RACE OF 2026 The season had not yet had a wet race where the 2026 cars could be tested and the rain - which had stayed away in practice and qualifying - arrived with heavy showers sweeping across the circuit, delaying the start. After a suspended start procedure, the second start had drivers split between intermediate and slick tyres but it was the former that thrived early in the race. When the lights went out, Antonelli accelerated through the middle from third on the grid to take the lead from Verstappen while Russell shot past on the outside to move up from seventh to second. But Verstappen's recovery began on lap six when he attacked Russell, overtaking the Briton by diving down the inside of turn four to set his sights on Antonelli. The Italian had to defend his position until lap 10 when Valtteri Bottas spun his Cadillac into the gravel, bringing out the safety car as Verstappen pitted while the two Mercedes cars double stacked to switch to slick tyres. VERSTAPPEN TAKES LEAD When the safety car came in, Verstappen stayed glued to Antonelli's rear tyre before overtaking the Italian on turn three, with Russell also surging past his team mate on the next turn to flip the order. Verstappen looked comfortable setting the pace up front as he set fastest laps and extended his lead over Russell to over four seconds as a frustrated Antonelli informed the team that he had the pace to chase the Dutchman. An impatient Antonelli overtook Russell on lap 21 to move up to second while behind them Hamilton had quietly been chipping away on his ageing soft tyres to move up to fifth behind Hadjar. But Antonelli missed his braking point at turn 15 and went briefly off track, hitting the pit lane bollard and costing him valuable time as Verstappen extended his lead to eight seconds. When the second safety car came out towards the end for Alex Albon's Williams that was stuck in the gravel, Russell suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he got out of the car with a suspected power unit issue.

Source: Reuters

Oct 4 : Croatia's Luka Modric said he was ashamed of his side's performance after they lost 7-0 to England in Rijeka on Saturday, the heaviest defeat in their history. Croatia's previous heaviest loss was a 6-0 defeat by Spain in 2018. Modric, the country's most-capped player, said the manner of the defeat by England was unacceptable. "It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance without duels, fouls, aggressiveness, togetherness... I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time I feel ashamed after a game," he told Jutarnji. "You can lose, or play against an opponent who is better - and they are right now. But in any case, losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable.

FAST

PHUKET: The United States aircraft carrier George H W Bush arrived in Thailand's resort island of Phuket on Sunday (Oct 4) with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East.

For the last six months, the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier and its strike group supported Operation Epic Fury and the US naval blockade in the US Central Command area of responsibility to secure maritime security and stability in the Middle East, according to the US Navy.

Phuket is the first port call for the George H W Bush Carrier Strike Group since departing Norfolk, Virginia, and Mayport, Florida, in March, the US Navy said in a statement.

Sailors will take part in cultural and community activities in Phuket, including sightseeing tours and a US-Thailand soccer match, it said.

The carrier anchored offshore, while crew members are expected to come ashore through Phuket Deep Sea Port and spend time on the popular southern resort island from Oct 4 to 9, local media reported.

Some sailors were seen coming ashore by boat.

The visit follows a five-day port call by the US carrier Abraham Lincoln at Laem Chabang in eastern Thailand last month, with about 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard.

A local mayor had estimated each US service member from the Lincoln could spend up to 3,000 baht ($89) per day during the visit.

Thailand is the United States' only treaty ally in mainland Southeast Asia.

FAST

RIYADH/DUBAI, Oct 4 : Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it. The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM. NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was no longer a priority, and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled.

However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely. NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority. The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction. RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format. Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities.  MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters.  According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold".  The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033. Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis. Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it expected a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6 per cent following a drop in oil activities. PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added. In January Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba. Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy later articulated by Saudi officials. Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The Aramco Stadium in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale. Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

Source: Reuters

SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ordered a thorough investigation and response measures over recent personal data leak incidents at banks, finance companies and public agencies, Seoul's presidential office said on Sunday (Oct 4).

Financial Services Commission (FSC) Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting with financial industry associations, regulators and executives from affected institutions on Sunday, warning that the sector must respond with the highest level of vigilance, the FSC said in a statement.

The FSC's Lee said authorities could not rule out the possibility that artificial intelligence was used in the attacks and called for an "AI attacks defended by AI" approach, while also signalling broader upgrades to the financial sector's cybersecurity framework.

Sunday's meeting came after similar talks on Friday, when the FSC said Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and others had reported cyberattacks, while Yonhap news agency reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank had also suffered breaches.

The banks could not immediately be reached for comment outside regular working hours on Sunday.

The financial regulator said authorities had launched on-site investigations after Shinhan Bank reported a breach on Sep 30 and had since expanded probes into other reported incidents.

The regulator directed financial institutions to carry out comprehensive security inspections, tighten access controls, minimise external system access and strengthen consumer protection measures.

It also said attack methods, internet protocol addresses and other threat information would be rapidly shared across the industry to prevent further incidents.

Yonhap news agency said regulators believe the attacks may have broadly scanned multiple financial companies for vulnerabilities rather than targeting a single institution.

Attack traffic was reported to have originated from IP addresses across several countries including the United States, Japan, Singapore, Vietnam and Britain, Yonhap said, citing bank data submitted to lawmakers.

Sunday's emergency meeting was brought forward from Oct 7 after additional breaches were discovered at second-tier financial institutions, according to multiple Korean media reports.

The country's main opposition People Power Party said authorities should also investigate the possibility of North Korean involvement, citing past cyberattacks attributed to Pyongyang against South Korean financial institutions.
